lessons.title: sh
lessons.goal: Read and spell words with the digraph `sh` at the start and end of words.
lessons.review: all Level 1 single letters, especially `s` and `h` (which combine to make this new sound)

A.text: Dad and I go to the shop. Dad gets fish for us, and a dish for Mom. "The shop is shut at six," Dad says. I wish for a big ship in the tub! Mom can put cash in a box for the shop. "It is on the shelf," Mom says.

B.text: Sam has a job at the fish shop. He gets cash for his boss, and fish for the shop. "The shop is shut at six," Sam's boss says. Sam and his mom wish for ten fish. "It is on the shelf, not in his bag," Sam says.

listen.passage: A fisherman named Tom worked on a small boat every morning. One day, Tom caught a fish that was absolutely **enormous** — far bigger than any fish he had ever seen before. It was so large that he could barely lift it into the boat! Tom's friends at the harbor could not believe their eyes. "That fish is enormous!" they shouted. Tom laughed and said an enormous fish like that would feed the whole street for a week. He shared it with every family on his road, and everyone had a wonderful dinner that night.

heart.note: heart part: the whole word is irregular for a beginning reader — it is spelled like it should rhyme with "days" or "plays," but it actually rhymes with "fez" (/sɛz/). Mark the whole word as heart for now. Point out it is the closest sibling of the Level 1 heart word "said" — both are the "tell/ask" word family and both break the same way.

heart part: the whole word is irregular for now (it needs the r-controlled `or` sound this course doesn't formally teach until Level 4); mark it fully heart, and note it sits right beside "of" — a Level 1 heart word the learner already knows — as a small memory anchor.

lessons.title: ch, tch
lessons.goal: Read and spell words with `ch` (start, middle, or end) and `tch` (end of a one-syllable word, right after a short vowel).

A.text: Min and Dad chat on the step. "Where did you go?" Min asks. "I ran to fetch the cat," Dad says. The cat sat in the hutch. Min and Dad catch the cat and shut the hutch. Min and Dad chat and chat. Min is rich in fun, if not in cash!

B.text: Sam and his boss chat at the shop. "Where did you go?" the boss asks. "I had to fetch cash for the shop," Sam says. Sam has a job at ten. Sam's boss is not rich, but the shop is a big shop. Sam and his boss chat, and Sam rushes to catch the bus.

listen.passage: A little cat named Pip was very **curious**. Every single day, Pip wanted to know what was happening on the other side of the garden wall. One afternoon, Pip's curious nose led her straight into a bush, where she found a family of hedgehogs curled up asleep! Pip was so curious that she gently poked one with her paw. The hedgehog woke up, uncurled, and gave a tiny, surprised squeak. Pip jumped back, but she was still curious — she sat and watched the hedgehogs for the rest of the afternoon, learning something new about her garden.

heart.note: heart part: the whole word is irregular for a beginning reader (it contains `th`, not taught until next lesson, plus an irregular `ere`); mark it fully heart for now, note it points to a place ("put it there").

heart part: same story as "there" — contains `wh` (not taught until L2.04) plus the same irregular `ere` ending; mark it fully heart, and point out "there" and "where" rhyme and share a spelling chunk, which helps memory.

lessons.title: th (voiced and unvoiced)
lessons.goal: Read and spell words with `th`, in both its sounds: unvoiced /θ/ (think, bath) and voiced /ð/ (this, then).

A.text: Min and Dad were at the bath. "Where were you?" Mom asks. "I ran from the path to fetch this," Dad says. Min sits in the bath with a thin moth. "Can a moth swim in a bath?" Min asks. "Not this moth," Dad says, "but you can!"

B.text: Sam and his boss were at the shop. "Where were you?" his boss asks. "I ran from the bus stop to fetch this," Sam says. Sam sits and acts fast. "I can fix this fast," Sam says. His boss sits, then says, "I will check on this and fix it fast."

listen.passage: Grandpa was usually calm, but one afternoon he got absolutely **furious**. His favorite garden tools had gone missing from the shed, and he was sure someone had taken them without asking. He searched the whole yard, muttering to himself, getting more and more furious with every empty corner. Then his granddaughter walked out holding the tools. "I borrowed them to fix my bike, Grandpa — I forgot to tell you!" she said. Grandpa's furious face softened into a small smile. "Next time," he said, "just tell me first, and I won't have to get furious over nothing."

heart.note: heart part: the whole word is irregular (sounds like "her" without the r-sound the spelling suggests); mark the entire word as heart for now, note it often follows "we/you/they" (we were, they were).

heart part: irregular for now (the `o` says an unexpected short-u-like sound, and it sits right after `fr`, a blend not formally taught until L2.06); mark the whole word as heart, note it pairs naturally with "to" (a Level 1 heart word) — "from here to there."

lessons.title: wh
lessons.goal: Read and spell words that start with `wh`.
lessons.newToday: `wh` (usually the plain /w/ sound; a few speakers/dialects say a puff-of-air /hw/ — either is acceptable)

A.text: Min asks Mom, "When will Dad come back?" "Dad will come back at six," Mom says. "Which mug is for some milk?" Min asks. "This mug," Mom says, and fills it with milk. Min sits and grins. When Dad comes back, Min claps and grins.

B.text: Sam asks his boss, "When will the cash come in?" "The cash will come in at six," his boss says. "Which bin is for some of the stock?" Sam asks. "This bin," his boss says, and fills it with stock. Sam sits and grins. When the cash comes in, Sam claps and grins.

listen.passage: Little Ana loved puzzles more than anything, but one rainy afternoon she found herself completely **puzzled**. Her grandmother had given her a box with no picture on the lid and no instructions inside — just three hundred loose pieces. Ana sat there, puzzled, turning pieces over in her hands, unsure where to even begin. She tried the edges first, but she was still puzzled about which piece connected to which. Finally, her grandmother sat beside her and said, "When you are puzzled, start with the corners — there are only four, and they always fit first." Ana found a corner, then another, and slowly her puzzled frown turned into a grin.

heart.note: heart part: the `o` says a short-u sound instead of the expected short o, and the final `e` is silent and doesn't make the vowel long (which will look odd once VCe is taught in Level 3 — flag that now: "come" is a real exception to the Level-3 silent-e rule, worth remembering). Mark only `o` + the silent `e` as heart.
same heart pattern as "come": `s` is regular, `om` sounds like short-u + m, final `e` silent. Point out "come" and "some" rhyme and share the same irregular spelling pattern — one memory, two words.

lessons.title: ng, nk
lessons.goal: Read and spell words ending in `ng` and `nk`.
lessons.newToday: `ng` /ŋ/, `nk` /ŋk/ (both are single sound-units at the end of a syllable, right after a vowel)
lessons.review: `sh, ch, tch, th, wh`; Level 1 letters

A.text: Min sings a song. "I want a pink hat," Min says. "When the song is done, you can have a pink hat," Dad says. Min sings and sings until the song is done. Dad claps, and hangs a pink hat on Min.

B.text: Sam wants his job done fast. "When is the job done?" his boss asks. "It is done at six," Sam says. Sam picks up his bag and a pink tin king from a bin. "This king is done for," Sam says, and grins. Sam wants to fix it, but the king is just junk.

listen.passage: After a full day at the farm, feeding the animals, mending fences, and carrying heavy buckets of water, farmer Iqbal was completely **exhausted**. His arms ached, his legs felt like stone, and he could barely climb the steps to his own porch. His son offered to finish the last chore, but Iqbal was too exhausted even to explain what needed doing — he just pointed and nodded. He sat down, closed his eyes, and within minutes he was fast asleep in his chair, still wearing his muddy boots. When he woke an hour later, he felt much better, though still a little exhausted, and very glad his son had taken care of the rest.

heart.note: heart part: `o` says a short-u sound (as in "come/some" from L2.04) and the final `e` is silent; mark `o`+silent-e as heart, `d` and `n` are fully regular.
heart part: `a` says an unexpected sound (closer to short o than short a); mark only the `a` as heart, `w`, `n`, and `t` are fully regular and already known.

lessons.title: Initial blends (st sp sn sm sl sw sk sc bl cl fl gl pl br cr dr fr gr pr tr tw)
lessons.goal: Read and spell words that start with a two-consonant blend, keeping both consonant sounds distinct (unlike a digraph, both letters keep their own sound).
lessons.newToday: initial blends `st sp sn sm sl sw sk sc` (s-blends) and `bl cl fl gl pl br cr dr fr gr pr tr tw` (l-blends and r-blends)
lessons.review: `sh, ch, tch, th, wh, ng, nk`; Level 1 letters

A.text: Min and Dad go to the pond. / "Can we swim?" / Min asks. / "Push the flip flops on fast," / Dad says. / A frog sits on a black rock. / Min wants to grab it, / but the frog can hop and skip fast! / "Let's clap and stomp," / Min says, / "then we can swim." / Dad and Min swim, / and Min wants to put the flip flops on the rock.

B.text: Sam must push to get the shop's stock done. / He picks up a black pen / and jots the stock on a pad. / A big box hits the step, / and Sam has to dash and shut it fast. / "I still must push to get this done," / Sam says, / "but a big box will not stop me." / Sam sits, / and gets the job done. / Sam wants to put the pen back on the desk.

listen.passage: Before crossing the busy market road, Aunt Rukhsana was always very **cautious**. She would stop at the edge, look left, then right, then left again, even if the road looked completely empty. Her nephew used to tease her about being so cautious, saying it took forever just to cross one small street. One evening, though, a bicycle came speeding around the corner at exactly the moment they stepped off the curb — and because Aunt Rukhsana had been cautious and was watching closely, she pulled her nephew back just in time. After that, her nephew never teased her again. "Better cautious than sorry," she always says, and now he says it too.

heart.note: heart part: the `u` says a short-oo sound (like "push," not like "cut"); mark only the `u` as heart, `p` and `t` are fully regular.
same `u` heart pattern as "put" — point out they rhyme in that one vowel sound; `p`, `sh` are fully regular (and `sh` review from L2.01).

rule.title: Blends
rule.text: Two consonants side by side keep BOTH sounds. Say them quickly, one after the other. FLOSS: after a short vowel at the end of a short word, f, l, s and z are doubled: stuff, smell, glass, buzz.

A.label: st, sp, sn, sm, sl, sw

B.label: st, sp, sn, sm, sl, sw

lessons.title: Final blends (-st -nd -nt -mp -sk -lt -ft -lk)
lessons.goal: Read and spell words that end in a two-consonant blend.
lessons.review: initial blends; `sh, ch, tch, th, wh, ng, nk`; Level 1 letters

A.text: Dad and Min set up a tent on the sand. / Min helps Dad pull the tent up. / "Pull fast!" / Dad says. / Min pulls and pulls until the tent is up. / Dad packs the milk and a gift in a bag. / Min helps hunt for the best spot to camp. / At dusk, / Min and Dad sit and rest, / full and glad.

B.text: Sam must pull the stock bin to the desk. / "Pull it fast," / his boss says. / Sam pulls and pulls until the bin is at the desk. / Sam checks the list, / packs the gift, / and gets it done. / The shop is full of stock, / and Sam is glad the job is done.

listen.passage: When the school bake sale raised more money than anyone expected, the head teacher decided to give every extra rupee to the small clinic down the road. She was **grateful** — truly grateful — for how hard the students had worked, baking and selling from early morning until the last plate was empty. One student asked why she looked close to tears. "I am just so grateful," she said. "You worked all day, and now families who could not afford medicine will get help." The students felt proud too, and decided that being the reason someone else got help was better than any prize. They planned an even bigger, more grateful bake sale for next year.

heart.note: heart part: same `u` sound as "put/push" from L2.06 (short-oo); point out the pattern repeats a third time; `p` and `ll` are fully regular.
same `u` heart pattern as "pull"; `f` and `ll` are fully regular.

rule.title: Final blends
rule.text: At the end of a word two consonants keep both sounds: nest, hand, jump. FLOSS still holds: a short vowel then f, l, s or z at the end doubles it.

lessons.title: Three-letter blends (str spr scr spl squ shr thr)
lessons.goal: Read and spell words that start with a three-consonant blend.
lessons.newToday: `str spr scr spl squ shr thr`
lessons.review: 2-letter initial and final blends; `sh, ch, tch, th, wh, ng, nk`; Level 1 letters

A.text: "Who has a shrimp and a squid?" / Min asks. / "Min has a shrimp and a squid," / Dad says. / "Could we splash them in the sink?" / Min asks. / "You could splash them in the tub," / Dad says. / Min and Dad splash the shrimp and squid in the tub. / Min grabs a strap and helps scrub the tub. / "This is a thrill!" / Min says, / and grins.

B.text: "Who could help scrub the shop?" / Sam's boss asks. / "I could," / Sam says, / and grabs a strap to fix the bin. / Sam splits the job with a pal. / Sam scrubs the mats, / and checks the straps on the bin. / Sam thinks the shop is strict but fun. / At the end, / Sam is glad the job is done.

listen.passage: A young dog named Bruno was usually eager to try anything new, but the first time his owner brought out a bicycle, Bruno was strangely **reluctant**. He backed away, tail low, refusing to go anywhere near the strange spinning wheels. His owner tried treats, gentle words, even a favorite toy — but Bruno stayed reluctant, watching from a safe distance. Then one afternoon, the owner simply sat beside the bicycle and let Bruno sniff it in his own time, with no pushing at all. Slowly, Bruno's reluctant ears perked up, and he stepped closer. By the end of the week, the once-reluctant Bruno was trotting happily alongside the bicycle on every walk.

heart.note: heart part: the whole word is irregular — `wh` here says /h/, not the usual /w/ from L2.04, and `o` says /oo/; mark the whole word as heart, but tell the learner explicitly it's the ONE exception to the `wh`=`/w/` rule they just learned, so they don't doubt the rule itself.

heart part: irregular vowel spelling and a silent `l`; only the final `d` is fully regular. Point out "could" rhymes with "would" and "should," coming in the next two lessons — same heart pattern, three words.

rule.title: Three-letter blends
rule.text: s plus a blend: three sounds said quickly, s-t-r in strap. shr and thr start with one digraph sound.

A.label: str, spr, scr, spl, squ, shr

B.label: str, spr, scr, spl, squ, shr

lessons.title: Adding -s and -es (plural and 3rd-person endings)
lessons.goal: Read and spell words with the `-s` and `-es` endings, and know the rule for which one a word needs.
lessons.newToday: the `-es` spelling rule (after `s, x, z, ch, sh`, add `-es` instead of plain `-s`, because you cannot say two hissing/buzzing sounds in a row without a vowel between them)
lessons.review: all blends and digraphs so far; the plain `-s` ending (already taught in Level 1)

A.text: Min washes the dishes and stacks the boxes. / "Would you help with the mugs?" / Mom asks. / "I would," / Min says, / and picks up the mugs. / "Should I stack them fast?" / Min asks. / "You should stack them fast," / Mom says. / Min washes, / stacks, / and fixes the mugs / until the job is done.

B.text: Sam fixes the vans and checks the boxes. / "Would you help me?" / his boss asks. / "I would," / Sam says, / and picks up the boxes. / "Should we stack them fast?" / Sam asks. / "You should stack them fast," / his boss says. / Sam checks, / stacks, / and fixes the vans / until the job is done.

listen.passage: When the class hamster went missing from its cage on a Friday afternoon, every student was **delighted** to hear it had been found safe behind the bookshelf on Monday morning. The teacher was delighted too, and let the whole class take turns holding it gently, one by one. One boy, who had been especially worried all weekend, was so delighted that he asked if he could bring the hamster home just for one night, to make sure it was really okay. His teacher smiled at how delighted — and relieved — he looked, and said yes, as long as his parents agreed. That evening, the whole family took turns being delighted by the tiny hamster running on its wheel.

heart.note: heart part: irregular vowel spelling and a silent `l`; only the final `d` is fully regular. Point out "would" rhymes with "could" (L2.08) and "should."
same heart pattern as "would"/"could." Three rhyming heart words (could, would, should) taught across three lessons — point this out explicitly; one memory pattern covers all three.

rule.title: Adding -s and -es
rule.text: Add -s to most words: cat, cats. Add -es after s, x, z, sh, ch and tch: it adds a syllable you can hear, wish, wishes.

lessons.title: Adding -ed (three sounds: /t/ /d/ /ɪd/)
lessons.goal: Read and spell words with the `-ed` ending, in all three of its sounds.
lessons.newToday: `-ed` says `/t/` (after an unvoiced sound: jump**ed**), `/d/` (after a voiced sound: grinn**ed**), or `/ɪd/` (after `t` or `d`: want**ed**, end**ed**) — one spelling, three sounds, and none of them is "ed" said as its own syllable except the `/ɪd/` case.
lessons.review: `-s/-es`; all blends and digraphs so far

A.text: Min jumped and jogged for fun. / "Did you want your bag?" / Mom asked. / "I packed four mugs in it," / Min said. / Min packed four mugs in a bag, / and rested on the step. / "You packed your bag fast," / Mom said, / and hugged Min. / Min grinned and rested, / glad the job was done.

B.text: Sam checked and fixed the vans. / "Did you want your list checked?" / his boss asked. / "I checked four vans," / Sam said. / Sam packed his bag, / and rested for ten. / "You fixed your job fast," / his boss said, / and grinned. / Sam packed, / jogged off, / and rested, / glad the job was done.

listen.passage: Uncle Hamid had asked his nephew, Bilal, to water the plants every single day while he was away — just that one job. When Hamid came home a week later and found every plant wilted and brown, he was **stubborn** about not letting it go. "It's just water, once a day," he said, again and again, refusing to accept Bilal's excuses about being busy with exams. Bilal, just as stubborn, insisted exams mattered more than plants. Neither would budge for two whole days. Finally, Hamid's wife stepped in and pointed out that both of them were being equally stubborn over something they could fix together in ten minutes. They laughed, apologized, and replanted the garden side by side that weekend.

heart.note: heart part: the whole word is irregular for a beginning reader (it needs the r-controlled vowel this course doesn't formally teach until Level 4); for now, mark it fully heart, note it means "belonging to you."
heart part: same story — irregular for now, taught properly in Level 4; mark it fully heart, note it's the number after three.

rule.title: Adding -ed
rule.text: -ed says /t/ after p k f s sh ch (jumped), /d/ after voiced sounds (grinned), and /ed/ after t or d (wanted).

lessons.title: Adding -ing and -er (no base change)
lessons.goal: Read and spell words with `-ing` (an action happening now) and `-er` (the person or thing that does it, or "more"), where the base word needs no spelling change at all.
lessons.newToday: `-ing`, `-er` (added straight onto the end — no doubling, no dropping letters; those spelling rules are their own lesson later, in Level 4)
lessons.review: `-ed`; `-s/-es`; all blends and digraphs so far

A.text: Min is packing and stacking many bags. / "Are you helping her?" / Mom asks Dad. / "I am helping her fast," / Dad says. / Min is filling and checking any bag Dad hands her. / "You are a fast helper," / Dad says. / Min is still packing, / glad to help.

B.text: Sam is checking and fixing many vans. / "Are you helping her?" / his boss asks. / "I am helping her fast," / Sam says. / Sam is stacking and packing any bin his boss hands her. / "You are a fast helper," / his boss says. / Sam is still checking, / glad to help.

listen.passage: The night before her first big exam, Ayesha felt more **anxious** than she had ever felt before. Her stomach fluttered, her hands felt cold, and she kept checking the clock, worried she was somehow forgetting something important. Her older sister noticed how anxious she looked and sat down beside her. "Being a little anxious means you care," her sister said, "but let's make a short plan so the anxious feeling has less to hold onto." Together they wrote down exactly what Ayesha needed for the morning, checked it twice, and set two alarms. Ayesha still felt a bit anxious as she fell asleep, but far less than before — and in the morning, she walked into the exam room calm and ready.

heart.note: heart part: `a` says a short-e-like sound instead of the expected short a, and the final `y` acts as a vowel (a Level 3 topic) — mark the whole word as heart for now.
same heart pattern as "many": `a` says an unexpected sound, final `y` as vowel; point out they share the same irregular chunk `an-`.

heart part: the whole word is irregular for now (it needs the r-controlled vowel this course doesn't formally teach until Level 4); mark it fully heart, note it means "belonging to her" or "that person," and it's the most common word so far that needs this specific r-controlled sound.

rule.title: Adding -ing and -er
rule.text: Read the base word, then add the ending. The base word does not change: jump, jumping, jumper.

lessons.title: Compound words and closed 2-syllable words
lessons.goal: Read and spell compound words (two whole words stuck together: *sunset*) and closed-syllable 2-syllable words (*rabbit, napkin*) by splitting them into two readable chunks first.
lessons.newToday: compound words; the VC/CV 2-syllable split (find the vowel in each half, split between the two middle consonants, read each closed syllable on its own, then blend the two chunks together)
lessons.review: everything so far — this lesson is the first time all of it gets used inside a single longer word

A.text: Min packs a backpack / for a picnic. / Does Min pack a napkin? / Min packs a napkin / and a muffin. / Dad packs two bits of catfish. / Min spots a rabbit / and a magnet in the grass. / Dad and Min sit / and watch the sunset. / Min goes to get the picnic bag, / then goes back to sit with Dad. / "Let's have a picnic," / Min says, / and Dad grins.

B.text: Sam packs his backpack / for his shift. / Does Sam pack a magnet? / Sam packs a magnet / for fixing the bus panel. / Sam checks for an insect problem / in the back bin. / Sam fixes a dent with the magnet trick. / This shop had a contest / for the best fix. / Sam goes to get his kit, / then goes back to fix the last dent. / At sunset, / the job is done, / and Sam packs up, / glad and full.

listen.passage: A wealthy trader in the old bazaar was known across the whole street for being unusually **generous**. Every evening, before he closed his stall, he would give away whatever fruit and bread had not sold that day — never selling it cheap at the last minute, always simply giving it to whoever needed it most. His neighbors thought he must be losing money, but the trader just smiled and said being generous had brought him more good luck and more loyal customers than any clever deal ever had. One winter, when his own stall caught fire, every single family he had once helped showed up the next morning with tools, wood, and cash to help him rebuild — proof, he said, that generous kindness always finds its way back.

heart.note: heart part: the whole word is irregular for a beginning reader (`o` says a short-u sound, `es` says just /z/); mark it fully heart for now, note it's the "he/she/it" form of "do" (a Level 1 heart word).

heart part: the whole word is irregular (`o` says its own name-ish sound via a silent-e-like pattern not yet taught, `es` says /z/); mark it fully heart, note it's the "he/she/it" form of "go" (a Level 1 heart word).
heart part: the whole word is irregular (the `w` is silent, and the spelling doesn't match the sound at all); mark it fully heart, note it's the number after one.

rule.title: Two-syllable words
rule.text: Find the two vowels. Split between the two consonants in the middle: rab·bit, nap·kin. Read each part, then the whole word.

A.label: bb, dd, gg, mm, nn, pp

B.label: bb, dd, gg, mm, nn, pp

lessons.title: Review (everything from Level 2)
lessons.goal: Consolidate every grapheme and ending taught in Level 2 before the mastery check — no new phonics content today, just cumulative retrieval practice at the hardest level the learner has reached.
lessons.review: `sh, ch, tch, th, wh, ng, nk`; initial and final 2-letter blends; 3-letter blends; `-s/-es, -ed, -ing/-er`; compounds and closed 2-syllable words
lessons.heartLine: again, friend, because (the last 3 of Level 2's 29)

A.text: Min and Dad go to visit a friend. / They pack a backpack with a napkin / and a muffin. / "I want to bring the pink rabbit," / Min says, / "because it is fun." / Min and the friend run and jump in the grass. / When they get to the pond, / they sit still. / A fish splashes, / and Min spots an insect on a twig. / The friend is helping Min hunt for bugs. / "Should we catch it?" / the friend asks. / "No, / let's just watch it," / Min says, / "because it is not bad." / They pack up at sunset, / and hug the friend. / Min and Dad go back, / glad and full, / and plan to come again.

B.text: Sam has a shift with a friend from a shop, / helping fix a big backlog of dents and checks. / "This job is a lot, / but his friend can help," / Sam says, / "because two friends finish fast." / They pack the kit, / check the list, / and split the job up. / Sam's friend fixes the dents, / and Sam checks the vans / and prints the list. / At dusk, / the shop has a full stock of fixed vans / and a strong stack of finished checks. / "We should do this again," / Sam's friend says. / "Yes, / because it went fast and we still got it done," / Sam says, / and they clap hands, / glad and calm.

listen.passage: Retrieval passage: A stubborn old goat named Bella refused to leave the muddy field even when it started to rain hard. Her owner, cautious as always, did not want to drag a furious, wet goat across a slippery yard, so he waited, patient, under the barn roof. After an hour of stubborn standing in the rain, Bella finally got cold enough to trot inside on her own — no longer stubborn, just cautious about getting even wetter. Her owner laughed, dried her off, and said a stubborn goat always changes its mind eventually, as long as you stay cautious and let it happen in its own time.

heart.note: heart part: contains the vowel team `ai` (a Level 3 topic, not yet taught) and doesn't say the sound the learner would expect from it anyway; mark it fully heart for now.
heart part: the whole word is irregular (the `ie` says a short-e sound, very unusual); mark it fully heart. Point out this is a word worth extra practice simply because it is used so often.

heart part: the whole word is irregular (`au` says a short sound, final `se` says /z/); mark it fully heart. This is the last new heart word in Level 2 — all 29 are now taught (review the full list together once, aloud).

lessons.title: Level 2 Mastery Check
lessons.goal: Confirm the learner has met every Level 2 exit criterion before starting Level 3.
lessons.newToday: nothing — this is the gate, not a teaching lesson.

offline: Decoding passage (read aloud with the tutor)

ui.teachIntro: Here is a new spelling for a sound. Tap it to hear it.
ui.teachBlend: These letters keep both sounds. Say them quickly together.
ui.teachSuffix: This is an ending. Read the base word, then add the ending.
ui.teachExample: Here it is in a word.
ui.ruleIntro: Here is a rule that helps you read.
ui.attackIntro: A long word. Let's break it apart, step by step.
ui.attackPeel: Tap the parts at the start or end that you know.
ui.attackBlend: Tap each chunk to say it, then put them together.
ui.attackFlex: Is it a real word? If not, try the vowel the other way.
ui.masteryIntro: This is the check for the whole level. Do your best.
